approved: Illegal Logging Prohibition Amendment (Strengthening Measures to Prevent Illegal Timber Trade) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would update Australia's laws against illegal timber to make it harder for illegally harvested wood to enter the country and to support legal trade.
It would give regulators more enforcement options, including new strict liability offences, civil penalties for false information, and powers to test timber samples for their species and origin.
The bill would also require a review of the law's operation within five years of the changes starting, and allow the minister to make rules that can be updated as needed.
Consolidates offences and civil penalties from the regulation into the main Act for clarity.
Adds strict liability offences that can be handled through infringement notices.
Extends powers to monitor, investigate, and test regulated timber products, including under biosecurity and customs controls.
Requires importers and processors to give notice when regulated timber products arrive or are processed.
Allows the department secretary to demand information or audits to check compliance with due diligence.
Authorises publication of contravention details on the department's website and protects officials from civil proceedings when exercising powers.
Timber importers, processors of raw logs, and businesses dealing with regulated timber products would be affected, as well as the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry and the minister.
